question.question: Explain how you would design a RESTful API for a user authentication system. Walk through the key components, the token strategy you would choose, and at least two security considerations.
expected_points: HTTP methods and endpoint structure (POST /auth/login, POST /auth/register, POST /auth/refresh)
Token expiry and short-lived access tokens

candidate_answer: I'd use JWT-based authentication. The login endpoint would accept email and password, validate credentials against a hashed password in the database using bcrypt, then return a short-lived access token and a longer-lived refresh token. Access tokens would expire in 15 minutes, and clients use the refresh endpoint to get new ones. I'd also add rate limiting on the login endpoint to prevent brute-force attacks.

missing_points: Refresh token rotation (invalidating old refresh tokens on use)
Token storage guidance (httpOnly cookies vs localStorage)
evaluation_result.feedback: Good foundational coverage — JWT, bcrypt, refresh tokens, and rate limiting are all present. To strengthen the answer, mention refresh token rotation (invalidating the old refresh token each time a new one is issued) and explicit HTTPS enforcement. Discussing where to store tokens safely (httpOnly cookies to prevent XSS) would demonstrate production security depth.
